source.citation: Kanaga Africa Tours, Chefferies of the West, and the earlier chieftaincy records in this collection. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.description: The chiefdom of the Fulani (Peulh) theocracies of the north, ruled by a lamido.
attributes.palace: A lamido's palace has an audience hall, wall frescoes that illustrate the history of the kingdom, objects linked to the cult, and vestments, reflecting the grandeur of the lamido.
attributes.regions: The title lamido is used in the Far North, North and Adamawa regions.
attributes.related: See also the record on titles of traditional rulers.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Rey Bouba and Palace of Rey Bouba (CC BY-SA 4.0), French Wikipedia on the lamidat, and the Cameroon embassy page on the palace. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.place: Rey Bouba, a town in the Mayo-Rey Department of the North Region.
attributes.history: Centre of the Lamidat (sultanate) of Rey Bouba, a vassal state of the Yola (Adamawa) Emirate, which was itself a vassal of the Sokoto Caliphate.
attributes.people: The inhabitants, the Boubandjidda, were of Hausa-Fulani origin.
attributes.palace: The Palace of Rey Bouba is the seat of the lamidat and is built in local mud-brick architecture.
attributes.heritage: Entered in the UNESCO World Heritage tentative list as Le Lamidat de Rey-Bouba, and on Cameroon's indicative list of cultural heritage.
attributes.first_ruler: French Wikipedia names Bouba Ndjidda as the first known ruler and says he came from the region of Mali.

source.citation: South African History Online, Cameroon. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.emergence: A more centralised state emerged around the Mandara Mountains in northern Cameroon at the end of the 1400s.
attributes.names: Sometimes called the Mandara Kingdom and sometimes the Wandala.
attributes.decline: It declined when Fulani people invaded in a jihad.
attributes.fulani_relations: The relationship was complicated: Mandara kings sometimes invited Fulani warriors to protect them from internal threats, so Fulani influence was large long before the final Fulani conquest in 1893.
attributes.related_heritage: The Diy-Gid-Biy Cultural Landscape of the Mandara Mountains was inscribed on the World Heritage List in July 2025.

source.citation: Tabletop Gaming, The armies of Rei Bouba, and the US State Department background note on Cameroon. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.late_18th_century: One account says a group of Fulani advanced south of Lake Chad in the late 18th century, drove people into the Mandara Mountains, and set up about sixty small emirates in the upland region that became known as Adamawa.
attributes.other_dating: The US State Department dates the Fulani conquest of most of northern Cameroon to between the late 1770s and the early 1800s.
attributes.caution: Sources give different dates and details.

source.citation: Soluap, List of Cameroon chiefs in the Far North and North. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.
